scienceRows.outcome: Baseline assessment (PythonAnywhere) — no new science content; unit starts W3
Compare animals with and without a backbone (vertebrates and invertebrates).
Explain how muscles work in pairs with bones to make the body move.
Identify that humans and animals need the right types and amount of nutrition.
Sort foods into groups and describe a balanced diet (links PSHE / Foodwise).
Explain that animals cannot make their own food; they get it from what they eat.
Describe how we can care for our environment: reduce, reuse and recycle (sustainability).
Compare and group rocks by their appearance and simple properties.
Test rocks for hardness and whether they let water through.
Identify everyday uses of different rocks (links D&T / Construction).
Group natural and human-made materials; record results in a table (ICT).
Plan and carry out a simple fair test on rocks.
Review and evidence learning on skeletons, nutrition & rocks (Entry Level Science / UAS).

scienceRows.outcome: Explain what fossils tell us about living things from long ago.
Recognise that soils are made from rocks and organic matter.
Compare different soils and how easily water passes through them.
Investigate which soil holds the most water; record results (ICT).
Recognise that we need light to see and that dark is the absence of light.
Identify sources of light and surfaces that reflect light.
Explain that the Sun's light can be dangerous and how to protect our eyes (links PSHE).
Investigate how shadows are formed when light is blocked.
Explore how the size of a shadow changes; record findings.
Plan and carry out a fair test about shadows or reflection.
Review and evidence learning on fossils, soils & light (Entry Level Science / UAS).

scienceRows.outcome: Describe the job of each part of a plant.
Identify what plants need to grow well (light, water, warmth, nutrients).
Plan an investigation into what plants need (links ASDAN allotment).
Set up and observe a plant-growth investigation over time (ICT to record).
Explain how water travels through a plant.
Compare how things move on different surfaces; explore friction (push and pull).
Identify contact and non-contact forces in everyday life.
Investigate which materials are magnetic and which are not.
Explore how magnets attract and repel, and find their poles.
Describe pollination and how flowers are pollinated (Plants B).
Explain how seeds form and are spread (seed dispersal).
Review the plant life cycle; evidence the year's science (Entry Level Science / UAS).
